newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania PM discusses boat victims with Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Albania PM discusses boat victims with Prodi.

text.p: Albania's interim Prime Minister Bashkim Fino pressed his Italian counterpart Romano Prodi on Friday on efforts to recover the bodies from a tragic shipping accident, his office said.

More than 100 people are thought to have drowned in March when a ship carrying Albanians fleeing the unrest in their troubled Balkan state collided with an Italian navy frigate 30 miles off Brindisi in southern Italy and sunk.
Fino's office said in a statement the premier told Prodi in a telephone discussion of his meeting with families of the Otranto victims and passed on their concern that the bodies be recovered.
It said Prodi emphasised his commitment to the recovery and explained the steps the Italian government had taken.

Prodi and Fino also discussed the work of the Italian-led eight nation force in Albania to secure humanitarian aid deliveries. Prodi stressed the readiness of the Italian troops to help with the reorganisation of the Albanian army and police, the statement said.

Prodi has twice visited neighbouring Albania since a 10-party National Reconciliation Government was set up in Tirana in March to halt the drift to anarchy following widespread unrest over the collapse of pyramid savings schemes.
Fino briefed Prodi on discussions between the parties on a law setting out the form of early elections, due by the end of June.

Fino's Socialists and other parties are at loggerheads with the Democratic Party, which ruled Albania before the crisis, over how many members of parliament should be elected by proportional representation.
Fino has threatened the resignation of the government if a draft approved by most parties is rejected by the Democratic Party -dominated parliament.
"Prodi paid special attention to holding elections in June by expressing his conviction that the necessary consensus would be achieved for that," the statement said.
